abstract: >
  [ABSTRACT TO BE WRITTEN AFTER RESULTS] We evaluate whether Brazil's
  fisheries restrictions — seasonal bans (defesos) and large marine protected
  areas — reduce total fishing pressure or displace effort across space,
  time, and species. We build a machine-readable registry of Brazilian
  fisheries regulations and link it to satellite-observed apparent fishing
  effort, enforcement records, and compensation payments (Seguro-Defeso).
  [RESULT TO BE GENERATED].

# Introduction

[Motivation: commons problem in fisheries; Brazil's regulatory mosaic of
seasonal bans and MPAs; the displacement critique — apparent local success
may hide spatial/temporal/species leakage. Contribution: (i) causal
estimates for a sharp offshore MPA creation (Decree 9,312/2018, Trindade
and Martim Vaz) and a real calendar shift in the Southeast/South shrimp
closure (Ordinance SAP/MAPA 656/2022); (ii) an explicit leakage
decomposition; (iii) a machine-readable fisheries regulation knowledge
base as reusable research infrastructure.]

# Institutional Background

[Brazilian fisheries governance: IBAMA/MMA/MPA competencies; defeso
instruments; Lei 11.959/2009; Seguro-Defeso (Lei 10.779/2003) unemployment
compensation; enforcement (IBAMA/ICMBio, infraction records); the 2018
large-MPA expansion (Decrees 9,312 and 9,313 of March 19, 2018).]

# Economic Theory and Mechanisms

[Common-pool resources; effort reallocation across margins (space, time,
species, gear); principal–agent enforcement; intertemporal substitution and
anticipation; compensation as reservation income vs. moral hazard; testable
implications H1–H8.]

# Information Systems Contribution

[People–process–technology view of the Fisheries Regulation Knowledge Base
and Spatial Compliance Observatory; atomic rule ontology; human-validated
extraction; versioned legal registry; exposure engine (cell × rule × date).]

# The Fisheries Regulation Knowledge Base

[Schema; provenance chain (official source, checksum); validation workflow;
descriptive statistics of the registry. Example: Ordinance 656/2022
structured as machine-readable rules, including its internal species-naming
inconsistency (Art. 2 §3) as a case study in legal-text ambiguity.]

# Data

[GFW apparent fishing effort (AIS; coverage caveats — artisanal fleet is
NOT observed); ICMBio/CNUC polygons via WFS; Seguro-Defeso microdata (CGU);
enforcement records; OISST environmental controls. Access dates and
checksums in the compendium.]

# Policy Selection

[Selection matrix (14 criteria, 6 candidates); why Trindade/Martim Vaz and
the 2023 shrimp-closure calendar shift.]

# Empirical Strategy

[Event study and spatial DiD with distance rings; synthetic DiD for the
single treated region; geographic RDD (conditional); calendar-shift
within-cell design; inference with few clusters (wild bootstrap,
spatial permutation).]
